newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua to function normally despite maintenance.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua to function normally despite maintenance.

text.p: The Brazilian port of Paranagua was functioning normally on Friday despite the closure of a bulk export terminal for routine maintenance work, a spokeswoman for the port said.
"The port is operating normally," the spokeswoman told Reuters. "Ships loading soybeans and soy products can use individual (privately-owned) terminals."
A port export terminal handling bulk goods, including soymeal, sugar, corn and beans, was closed for maintenance until February 15 in preparation of the new harvest, she said.
"It is a routine procedure required by law," the spokeswoman added.
She was not immediately able to confirm whether a ship scheduled to load 53,200 tonnes of soymeal this week, the Belchatom, had been able to complete loading.

Traders last week said the first of the early cycle soybean harvest was scheduled to leave Paranagua from February 15 but warned there could be delays because rains postponed the harvest in Mato Grosso state, where most of the early crop is planted.
Paranagua, located in the key soybean producing region of Parana, is the largest terminal in South America for loading grains.
